t: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Department of the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126), $2,700,000 are rescinded.

fable.w: This section only rescinds previously appropriated funds. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only rescinds previously appropriated funds. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. Because no outside party takes part in any federal decision, it is not participation.
opus.s: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Department of the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126), $2,700,000 are rescinded.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Nothing here tempts a "Yes." The section cancels $2,700,000 of previously appropriated funds. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply rescinds a portion of appropriated funds. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are Congress and the Department of the Interior, both of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Department of the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126), $2,700,000 are rescinded.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that rescinding funds is a "decision" and that the process leading to it involved participation. However, the text itself only describes the rescission of funds. It does not describe any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory board involving non-federal parties. The actors involved (Congress appropriating/rescinding, the Department of the Interior) are all inside the federal government.
